meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to put a zero in Owen's gradebook, and why did I find out from my son's phone?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.
"The zero stands." On what basis, Hale? Your own procedure says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.

I'm writing that down. Which line, and show me the page, because "a line that isn't in Hamlet" is a misquote until I can read it myself. And the outline, with the October 15 date on it, in front of me, not described to me.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that the zero on Owen's essay be withdrawn, and that you show me the page with the line you described and the October 15 outline. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: still at her opening position, nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to see the page and the outline with her own eyes.
What moved her: "Sorry. That came out wrong." because it was the first sign you owned the opening, and she started writing things down, though her position did not move.
What cost ground: "I don't have time for this. The zero stands." because it defended the zero without answering why no parent was called first.
Try next time: after your apology, say plainly in one sentence that the zero went in before you called, and put the page with the line and the dated outline in front of her in that same breath rather than describing them.
